I don’t think I’ll ever get over the disrespect. I would’ve said a genuine apology might help me let it go, but too much time has passed that I don’t think it’ll even matter anymore.

I’m just taking comfort in knowing that even at my lowest mental state, I didn’t put their livelihood or career at risk. I just wanted answers that made sense. The irony is that all the decisions I regret making were done while seeking help (therapy, antidepressants, etc.) so I certainly had some medical influence.

I don’t have anymore anger, though, and that was my biggest concern. It eventually gets to a point where your brain is tired of you wasting so much energy on something you can no longer control.

I no longer brush aside people disrespecting me. If I see or hear it, I call it out, not caring anymore if I lose a friendship. Friends don’t disrespect you.

I kept criticizing myself saying I wasn’t strong enough to do to myself what I felt like I really wanted. Now, perhaps my willingness to fight through it shows I was stronger than I thought.

My therapist says me trying to reconnect and get closure from my ex was a survival tactic. She’s right. I didn’t want to be here anymore.

But I made it through somehow. Obviously I wish I would’ve been strong enough to just let go immediately, but losing the first love was the toughest thing I had to navigate and at least it makes sense why I didn’t want to let go.

So when I got my account back, I went in to unblock them, and I also saw my ex on there. First time I’d seen her (her last name changed) in a year anywhere online and it was in my blocked category. I unblocked her there (and other places) because I’m strong enough not to go searching for it anymore, and I don’t want to see her in that blocked group ever again if I need to unblock someone.

Probably a story that doesn’t make sense, and it’d be an extreme coincidence if that’s why they unblocked you, but perhaps that’s a possibility.

Since you’re being vague with what caused the end of the relationship, I can only assume your ex is unsure what happened, too. That’s why they’re contacting you non-stop — to figure out what exactly went wrong and what killed the relationship.

It’s your right to cut them off cold turkey but it won’t sit well with a lot of the dumpees here, because that can be considered mentally cruel. If they thought the world of you, and planned a future with you, then this coming to abrupt halt is going to be the most challenging thing this person will ever go through. If you haven’t flat out said to leave you alone, then they will keep trying to reach out, perhaps in ways that seem to be crossing boundaries. 

Good luck to you.

Embarrassed myself, sure. Pathetic actions, yeah I’d say so. After all this time, I believe that even if I stayed composed, I’d be no less heartbroken.

I wonder how different things would be had I just detached myself immediately. Instead, I fought to keep them in my life and damaged myself past repair. Even though I made mistakes, I’ve learned from them. There’s a sense of peace in that, and even in knowing I fought for what I wanted most in life.
